The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act',
for short) has been filed by the claimant being aggrieved by the judgment dated 31.07.2019 passed by the II Addl.
Senior
Civil Judge and MACT, Chikkamagaluru (for short, 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.510/2017

. 
2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 22.03.2017 at about 5.30 p.m.,
the claimant was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-18/EB-2017 from Kadur to NC: 2023:KHC:40909 Chikkamagaluru.

When he reached near Chandregowda's house,
Laxmipura village, K.M.road, Chikkamagaluru, at that time, another motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 18/W-3015 being ridden by its rider at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner,
dashed to the vehicle of the claimant.

As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant fell down,
sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he spent huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance, etc.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred purely on account of the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider.

sentences.text: On service of notice, the respondent Nos.1 to 4 appeared through counsel and respondent Nos. 2 to 4 filed written statement in which the averments made in the petition were denied.

The age,
avocation and income of the claimant and the medical expenses are denied.
It was pleaded that the accident was due to the rash and NC: 2023:KHC:40909 negligent riding of the vehicle by the claimant himself.
It was further pleaded that the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimant is exorbitant.
Hence, they sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimant himself was examined as PW1, Dr.Venkatesh as PW2 and another witness as PW3 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P78.
On behalf of the respondents, two witnesses were examined as RW1 and RW2 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R8.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia

, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent riding of the claimant and also the offending vehicle by its rider at 50% each, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.2,91,441/- along with interest at the rate of 8%
p.a. and directed the owner of the offending vehicle to deposit 50% of the compensation amount,
i.e., Rs.1,45,721/-
NC: 2023:KHC:40909 along with interest.
Being aggrieved, this appeal has been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
(i) Firstly, even though the claimant claims that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken the notional income as only Rs.8,000/- per month.
(ii) Secondly, due to the accident, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries.
He was treated as inpatient for a period of 13 days.
Even after discharge from the hospital, he was not in a position to discharge his regular work.
He suffered lot of pain during treatment and he has to suffer the disability and unhappiness throughout his life.
Considering the same, the compensation granted by the Tribunal under the heads of 'loss of amenities', 'pain and sufferings' and other incidental expenses are on the lower side.
(iii) Thirdly, even though the rider of the offending vehicle was not having a valid and effective driving licence.

In respect of claimant is concerned, the Insurance NC: 2023:KHC:40909 Company has to pay the compensation at the first instance with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

In support of his contentions, he relied on the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of PAPPU AND OTHERS vs. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER reported in AIR 2018 SC 592 and a Full Bench judgment of this Court in the case of NEW INDIA ASSURANCE CO.
LTD.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following contentions:
(i) Firstly, even though the claimant claims that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, he has not produced any documents to establish his income.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the claimant notionally.
(ii) Secondly, the injuries suffered by the claimant are minor in nature.
He was inpatient for only 13 days.
Considering the evidence of the doctor and the injuries NC: 2023:KHC:40909 suffered by the claimant, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
(iii) Thirdly, it is not in dispute that the rider of the offending vehicle was not having a valid and effective driving licence.
Since insured has violated the policy condition the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.
The Tribunal has rightly exonerated the Insurance Company.

(iv) Fourthly, in view of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of MS.JOYEETA BOSE AND OTHERS vs. VENKATESHAN.V AND OTHERS (MFA 5896/2018 and connected matters disposed of on 24.8.2020), the interest granted by the Tribunal at the rate of 8% p.a. is on the higher side and the same has to be reduced to 6% p.a.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the judgment and award and the original records.

9. In respect of negligence is concerned, the Tribunal, after considering the evidence of the parties and NC: 2023:KHC:40909 the materials available on record, has rightly held that the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-18/EB- 2017 has contributed 50% to the accident and the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-18/W-3015 has contributed 50% to the accident.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled to only 50% of the compensation.
10. The claimant has not produced any evidence with regard to his income.
Therefore, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2017, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.11,000/- p.m.

Due to the accident the claimant has suffered fracture of right femur bone,
fracture of right 2nd and 3rd metacarpal bone and fracture of right 2nd and 3rd meta tarsal bone.
The Tribunal has rightly assessed the whole body disability at 6.66%.
The claimant was aged about 31 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '16'.

Thus, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,40,659/- (Rs.11,000*12*16*6.66%) on account of NC:
2023:KHC:40909 'loss of future income'.
Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injuries, he has suffered lot of pain during treatment and he has to suffer with the disability and unhappiness throughout his life.

Considering the same, I am inclined to enhance the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'pain and sufferings' from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.40,000/-
and 'loss of amenities' from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.40,000/-.

'loss of income during laid-up period' for a M.S. Sundaresh vs Jagadish on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136354690/
4 period of two months, i.e., Rs.22,000/- (Rs.11,000*2).
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is just and reasonable.

11. Thus, the claimant is entitled to the following compensation:

The Tribunal has given a finding that the rider of the offending vehicle was not having a valid and effective driving licence.
The Tribunal has rightly exonerated the Insurance Company from the liability.

However, in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of PAPPU (supra) and a Full Bench judgment of this Court in the case of YELLAVVA (supra), Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation at the first instance with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

13. In view of the above, I pass the following order:
M.S. Sundaresh vs Jagadish on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136354690/
5 (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:40909 (ii) The judgment of the claims Tribunal is modified.
The claimant is entitled to 50% of the total compensation of Rs.3,87,802, i.e., Rs.1,93,901/- in place of Rs.1,45,721/- awarded by the Tribunal.

(iii) The New India Assurance Company Limited, i.e., respondent No.3 herein is directed to deposit a sum of Rs.1,93,901/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment, excluding interest for the compensation awarded under the head of 'future medical expenses' at Rs.16,000/-,
with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-18/W- 3015.

(iv) The enhanced compensation carries interest @ 6% p.a. Sd/-
